incidents.title: Joyfill npm packages hijacked — import-time RAT with blockchain C2
incidents.summary: Malicious 2773-beta builds of @joyfill/components and @joyfill/layouts ship an obfuscated five-stage chain that runs the moment the module is imported, then resolves its C2 from a Tron transaction (pivoting to Binance Smart Chain) before opening a Socket.IO RAT and dropping a Python credential stealer. Payload executes at import time, so npm install --ignore-scripts does NOT stop it — the campaign marker A9-0135-3 and the C2 IPs are the durable catches.
incidents.action: Audit lockfiles/CI for any 2773 prerelease of the two packages; pin to a clean release published before Jul 28, remove the versions, rotate every credential on affected machines (Git/npm tokens, wallet keys, browser secrets), and block the C2 IPs and the Sec-V: A9-0135-3 header.

iocs.context: Campaign tag — sent as Sec-V HTTP header / embedded global marker
Tron dead-drop address for C2 resolution (also TXfxHUet9pJVU1BgVkBAbrES4YUc1nGzcG, TA48dct6rFW8BXsiLAtjFaVFoSuryMjD3v)

incidents.title: Flying Eagle Android RAT — leaked builder spawns 170 live servers
incidents.summary: The source for this SpyNote-class Android RAT leaked on criminal Telegram channels as a 388 MB archive (中国龙.zip); Hunt.io pivoted on its default TLS certificate and AdminPro panel fingerprint to find 170 active servers, HK-centric. It abuses Accessibility Services for gesture injection and overlay phishing against banking, Alipay and WeChat. The default Let's Encrypt cert (SHA-1 AB:42:24:...:7E:30) and the AdminPro login-redirect fingerprint catch panels network-wide even after operators rebrand.
incidents.action: Block the C2 domains/IPs below; hunt egress for the default TLS cert SHA-1 and the AdminPro /login?redirect=list/basic-list panel fingerprint; on MDM, alert when a sideloaded APK is granted Accessibility Service.

iocs.context: Default panel TLS cert (CN alcs.xyttkx[.]cc, Let's Encrypt R13, valid 2026-04-07 to 07-06)
Flying Eagle C2 (matches default cert CN)
Hardcoded default app id (randomized at build time)

incidents.title: Tengu botnet — Mirai-derived Linux malware that reboots hosts to survive cleanup
incidents.summary: A Mirai-derived, multi-architecture Linux botnet whose self-defense sets it apart: a guardian process re-checks the main binary every 60s, and it abuses the hardware watchdog so that killing the process forces a device reboot rather than a cleanup. Durable catch: a background process masquerading as [kworker/0:0] that reopens /dev/watchdog and sends keepalives — no legitimate userland process does this.
incidents.action: Block the C2 IP below; on Linux/IoT fleet hunt for a process named [kworker/0:0] holding /dev/watchdog, unexpected watchdog keepalives, and fake systemd/init persistence. No sample hashes were published — URLhaus URLs were already offline at disclosure.

iocs.context: Abused to force reboot (~30s timeout) when malware is killed

incidents.title: Dysphoria IoT botnet — blockchain-hidden C2, rebuilt in 6 days after takedown
incidents.summary: A JackSkid-descended IoT botnet (~200,000 devices) that resolves its command servers through Ethereum ENS and Solana SNS domains, with C2 addresses concealed inside fake IPv6 strings and recovered by a custom byte transform. It sells DDoS-for-hire up to ~4 Tbps. Durable catch: ENS/SNS name-service lookups originating from IoT/edge segments — a lookup no normal camera or router makes.
facts: ENS/SNS BLOCKCHAIN C2 · up to 4 Tbps
incidents.action: Alert on any ENS/SNS resolution from IoT/OT segments and block the blockchain domains below; patch CVE-2025-9528 (Linksys E1700), enforce strong telnet/SSH credentials, and disable UPnP on internet-facing edge devices.

iocs.context: Ethereum ENS domain — encodes distribution-node IPv4s
Linksys E1700 command injection — a spreading vector

incidents.title: VeilStealer — PowerShell infostealer with registry-run persistence
incidents.summary: A Windows credential stealer that leans on PowerShell for execution, plants a Run-key for autostart, harvests browser credentials, and exfiltrates over its C2 channel. CYFIRMA published eight sample hashes and a YARA rule. Network IOCs were not published, so the eight hashes plus the PowerShell-writes-Run-key behavior are the reliable catches.
incidents.action: Block the eight hashes and deploy CYFIRMA's YARA rule; hunt for PowerShell processes writing HKCU/HKLM Run keys and reading browser credential stores.

incidents.title: Laundry Bear — Russian Zimbra webmail XSS espionage (CISA AA26-204A)
incidents.summary: CISA and partners warned that Russian state-supported actor Laundry Bear has, since at least July 2025, exploited a Zimbra webmail XSS (CVE-2025-66376, insufficient sanitization of CSS @import in email) to silently exfiltrate ~90 days of mail plus Global Address Lists from Western government, defense and nuclear-sector targets. Triggered just by viewing a crafted email — hunt bulk outbound mailbox exports to VPS ranges and inbound mail containing CSS @import.
incidents.action: Patch ZCS to the Nov-2025 (or later) build; import the full IP/domain/hash set from the CISA AA26-204A STIX bundle; alert on large outbound mailbox exports to VPS providers, pass-the-cookie reuse, and inbound mail bodies containing CSS @import directives.

iocs.context: Zimbra ZCS webmail XSS (CSS @import) — patched Nov 2025, still exploited

iocs.value: CSS @import directive in inbound email body
iocs.context: View-based exploit trigger — flag/strip in mail gateway
Full IP / domain / hash IOC set — download from the CISA advisory

incidents.title: CVE-2026-16232 — Check Point SmartConsole authentication bypass
incidents.summary: An unauthenticated attacker with network access to a Check Point Security Management Server or MDS can read the server's SIC distinguished name over the bootstrap channel, replay it to log into SmartConsole with full administrator rights, and rewrite security policy. CVSS 9.1, exploited in the wild as a zero-day; Rapid7 has since published a PoC. Default Trusted-Clients config leaves GUI clients unrestricted — patch and lock it down now.
incidents.action: Emergency-apply Jumbo Hotfix R82.10 Take 36 / R82 Take 118; restrict Trusted Clients so GUI clients are not open by default; hunt for unauthenticated SIC bootstrap reads and unexpected SmartConsole admin logins / policy changes.

iocs.context: SmartConsole auth bypass — Security Management Server & MDS

iocs.value: Jumbo Hotfix: R82.10 Take 36 / R82 Take 118
iocs.context: Fixed builds — apply on an emergency basis

iocs.value: Unauthenticated SIC DN read then replay
iocs.context: Bootstrap channel reads mgmt SIC distinguished name, replayed for admin

incidents.title: CVE-2026-50522 — SharePoint deserialization RCE, machine-key theft
incidents.summary: An unauthenticated .NET deserialization flaw in on-prem SharePoint (2016 / 2019 / Subscription Edition) lets an attacker POST a crafted SecurityContextToken to /_trust/default.aspx and execute code as the server. Public PoC drove active exploitation; CISA added it to KEV on Jul 22 with a Jul 25 fix deadline. Attackers pull SharePoint machine keys in a single request, so patching alone is not enough — rotate ASP.NET machine keys.
incidents.action: Apply Microsoft's July SharePoint update, then ROTATE ASP.NET machine keys and restart IIS; monitor POSTs to /_trust/default.aspx and forged SecurityContextToken sign-ins, and hunt for new webshells under the SharePoint web root.

iocs.context: Exploited endpoint — POST target for the forged token
Malicious .NET payload in WS-Federation sign-in cookie
Patch is insufficient — rotate ASP.NET machine keys

incidents.title: SourTrade — malvertising that makes the browser assemble the malware in memory
incidents.summary: A malvertising operation impersonating TradingView, Solana and Luno serves no finished binary: its landing page pulls build instructions from /config, fetches a clean Bun runtime plus per-session AES-CTR bytes, assembles a unique Windows executable in browser memory, and hands it over through a ServiceWorker-controlled same-origin download. Every victim gets a different hash, so detection hinges on the /config build flow, the 96 domains, and the malicious JavaScriptCore bytecode in the PE's .bun section — not on a static hash.
incidents.action: Block the domains below; alert on browser-delivered same-origin downloads of PE files that carry a .bun section, and on pages that fetch a Bun runtime plus a /config template then assemble a download via ServiceWorker. The per-session hashes are near-useless for blocking on their own.

incidents.title: BlackSeeStealer — browser-credential stealer with a telltale User-Agent
incidents.summary: A Windows infostealer that raids credential stores across eight browsers — Chrome, Edge, Brave, Firefox, Opera, Vivaldi, Yandex and Tor — runs environment/sandbox checks first, stages loot into named text files, then exfiltrates over HTTP. Durable catch: the hardcoded User-Agent "IP Checker/1.0" and the staged UserInformation.txt / browser_decryption.log artifacts.
incidents.action: Block the hash; alert on the "IP Checker/1.0" User-Agent leaving the network and on creation of UserInformation.txt, browser_decryption.log, or installed_applications.txt in user temp/profile paths.

iocs.context: Exfiltration endpoint (HTTP POST of staged loot)
Legit geo/IP service used for recon — hunt in context, don't blanket-block (also api[.]ipify[.]org)
